artifacts.title: Bowen v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.

artifacts.title: Inactive or non-locally-elected elders as General Assembly commissioners

matches.evidence: A rotating-session inactive elder may be elected GA commissioner, but a ruling elder never elected in that congregation may not serve as its commissioner.

artifacts.title: Emeritus officers voting in higher courts and local bodies

matches.evidence: The CCB affirmed that an Elder Emeritus may not vote in the local session but may vote as a delegate to Presbytery if appointed to serve there.

artifacts.title: Voting rights of Elders and Deacons Emeriti after BCO 24-9 amendment

matches.evidence: The CCB noted that the Twelfth GA amended BCO 24-9 to prohibit Emeriti from voting, while a grandfather clause preserved prior voting privileges for those already holding them.

artifacts.title: Requiring ministers without call to report annually to presbytery

matches.evidence: An overture mandating annual presbytery reporting for officers without call was in conflict with the Constitution because the new BCO 34-10 language conflicted with BCO 42-2.

artifacts.title: Limiting TE voting rights in presbytery and General Assembly to pastors

matches.evidence: The CCB again found the overture in conflict with BCO 3-1 and 14-2, reaffirming that restricting voting to pastors disenfranchises non-pastor Teaching Elders.

artifacts.title: Restricting presbytery and General Assembly voting to pastors only

matches.evidence: The CCB found the overture in conflict with BCO 3-1, which vests church power in the whole body, and BCO 14-2, which entitles all TEs to representation.
